game: NYG @ DEN Week 7 2025, kickoff 2025-10-19 16:05 ET, outdoor, DEN -7.5, total 39.5

script.base: Market prices a controlled Denver lead: implied totals DEN 23.5 / NYG 16.0 in a low 39.5 outdoor game, so Denver leads by the half and closes with J.K. Dobbins (50 carries, 220 yards in weeks 4-6) rather than a shootout. Pace is moderate-slow. NYG, a 7.5 dog, throws more once behind, but a 16-point team total caps that volume. A 7.5 spread is a lead-and-run script, not an automatic Q4 benching of Dobbins.
script.flip1: NYG stays in it via Jaxson Dart's legs (27 carries, 169 rush yards in weeks 4-6) and Cam Skattebo's volume, so Denver never gets the clock-kill. Dobbins carries stall and Bo Nix has to throw, which lifts Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin and Evan Engram and keeps Skattebo on the field as a runner.
script.flip2: Denver scores early and it becomes garbage time. Dobbins' late snaps get cut, NYG abandons the run so Skattebo's rushing line dies, Denver WR yards stall, and NYG short passing (Wan'Dale Robinson, Theo Johnson) picks up empty volume.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report only; inactives ~90 min pre-kick are not in the pack. NYG C John Michael Schmitz is Out (concussion), so Giants pressure and negative rushing efficiency should rise and the quick game (RB/TE/slot) should gain while deep WR yards lose. NYG WR Darius Slayton is Doubtful (hamstring; 10 targets, 75 yards, 169 air in weeks 4-6), so if he sits the target vacuum goes to Robinson (already 19 targets), Johnson (16), Lil'Jordan Humphrey, Jalin Hyatt and Daniel Bellinger — lines have no saved prices, so a lag cannot be confirmed, and Doubtful is not a confirmed scratch. NYG DE Chauncey Golston is Doubtful (neck) and LB Abdul Carter is Questionable (hamstring), which softens the edge Denver runs and throws against; NYG LBs Demetrius Flannigan-Fowles (Out, hamstring) and Swayze Bozeman (Out, ankle), plus Victor Dimukeje Questionable (pectoral), are the linebacker group Evan Engram and RJ Harvey would attack. DEN LB Jonah Elliss is Out (shoulder), a small NYG pass-protection boost that only partly offsets Schmitz; DEN LB Dre Greenlaw is Questionable (quad) and would help NYG's short/middle game only if he sits. Malik Nabers is not on this report but has zero targets in the weeks 4-6 log, so his role is unconfirmed and he is not a leg.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location splits only: DEN defense YPA left 4.76 (74 throws), middle 6.47 (38), right 7.53 (77). NYG defense YPA left 7.05 (83), middle 7.21 (38), right 6.62 (104) — Giants bleed everywhere, worst in the middle.
matchup.pressure: DEN blitzes 32% and NYG EPA/dropback is worse when blitzed (-0.12) than when not (-0.05), and Schmitz is out, so Giants should live in quick throws. NYG blitzes 34%, but DEN EPA/dropback is +0.10 both blitzed and not, so Nix is not pressure-fragile; Golston Doubtful and Carter Questionable further lower the chance NYG's rush gets home.
matchup.bleeds: DEN run defense is the stingy unit: 3.94 YPC and only 6 runs of 10+ in 6 games, plus 13 passes of 20+ for 219 yards. NYG run defense is the bleed: 5.42 YPC and 25 runs of 10+ in 6 games, plus 14 passes of 20+ for 238 yards.
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Dobbins, the lead back in a Denver-lead script, into that 5.42 YPC / 25-explosive-run Giants front with Golston and Carter compromised. Second overlap is the Giants linebacker absences into Denver's underneath options (Engram 19 targets, Harvey 12 targets in weeks 4-6) and the middle at 7.21 YPA. NYG's own top option, Robinson (19 targets, only 88 air yards), fits the quick-game pressure script but runs into a Denver defense that is sound on the left (4.76 YPA) and does not bleed short yardage the way NYG does.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. Denver never led: Dart and Skattebo kept the Giants within a score, Nix threw downfield to Sutton (the 17-yard dud did not repeat; the 99-118 yard games did), and Dobbins was held to the 40-yard path because the 5.42 YPC figure was opponent-driven and Carter played through the questionable tag. Harvey's 40-yard receiving game was one play, Dobbins stayed in on third down, and Harvey finished at 14 again while Engram, not Harvey, took the linebacker mismatch. Separately, a late Slayton inactive or a surprise Denver inactive is not in this morning report, and an unsaved Denver wind forecast could have scrambled the screen timing without helping a yardage line that still needs catches. That counter is real on Harvey, which is why he is a lean, and real as a floor on Dobbins, which is why the strong read is flagged rather than sized. It is not stronger than the Dobbins matchup-plus-script read, so Dobbins stays.
slip_story: One story only: Denver lead-and-control against a soft Giants front seven. Dobbins rush over is the clock-kill anchor; Harvey rec over is the passing-down complement, not a shootout stack and not an opposite-script under. No TD legs, one market per player, two legs. Do not pair this with a game over, a Sutton over, or a Skattebo rush over. Re-check Golston, Carter, Greenlaw, Dimukeje and Slayton at inactives before any human decision.
